The eigenvalues of the system's matrix are ${\lambda }_{1}$ and ${\lambda }_{2},$ for which the corresponding eigenvectors are ${v}_{1}=[-1,\text{ }3]^{T}$ and ${v}_{2}=[1,\text{ }1]^{T},$ respectively.

worked_solution:
The straight-line solutions of the system have the form

$$
{c}_{1}{e}^{{\lambda }_{1}t}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\,\text{and}\,{c}_{2}{e}^{{\lambda }_{2}t}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

The line that passes through the origin and is parallel to ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]$ has the equation 

$$
y=-3x,
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14072827/assets/ed058963b391a4cdc66b2ab48483906a4d07759681c1f24e47ffc9e10775895f.png)

The tangents along this line are pointing $\text{toward the origin},$ meaning that the solutions of the form 
${c}_{1}{e}^{{\lambda }_{1}t}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]$
must approach $\text{the origin}$ as $t\to \infty .$ So, we must have ${\lambda }_{1}<0.$

The line that passes through the origin and is parallel to ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ has the equation 

$$
y=x,
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14072827/assets/6c92028370c86431ddc6ccd9513c273054d98b5add159e1bddf5a2e11751d987.png)

The tangents along this line are pointing $\text{away from the origin},$ meaning that the solutions of the form 
${c}_{2}{e}^{{\lambda }_{2}t}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$
must approach $\text{infinity}$ as $t\to \infty .$ So, we must have ${\lambda }_{2}>0.$

The straight-line solutions of the system have the form c1eλ1t[−13]andc2eλ2t[11].

The line that passes through the origin and is parallel to v1=[−13] has the equation y=−3x, as shown below.

The tangents along this line are pointing toward the origin, meaning that the solutions of the form c1eλ1t[−13] must approach the origin as t→∞. So, we must have λ1<0.

The line that passes through the origin and is parallel to v2=[11] has the equation y=x, as shown below.
